issue.title: gateway: a shorter rest overwrites a longer one, so a 1s 429 rest replaces a 30-min out-of-credit rest and the provider is retried every second
issue.body:
## What happens

When concurrent requests on one provider come back with different failures, the rest that is written last wins, even if it is shorter. A 1-second rate-limit rest can replace a 30-minute out-of-credit rest. The account is then tried again a second later, gets refused again, and the cycle keeps going.

We run [sub2tok](https://sub2tok.com), a gateway used through the `@sub2tok/magpie` provider plugin. One account with an almost-empty balance (below what a single request needs) sent about 3,400 refused requests over 6 hours from `magpie/0.1.1319`, in bursts of 2–3 requests every few seconds. In each burst:

- one request gets `402` with an `insufficient_balance` body → `failure()` classifies it as `failCredit` → rest `creditRest` (30 min)
- a request sent at the same moment gets `429` (`rate_limit_error`, `retry-after: 1`), because the first one is still holding the balance → `failRate` → rest ~1 s

Both replies arrive within ~100 ms. Whichever is written second sets `restingUntil.m[id]`, so the 30-minute rest is often replaced by a 1-second one.

## Where

`restAfterMarked` writes the rest without comparing it to the one already there:

https://github.com/yetone/magpie/blob/95be6bb/internal/gateway/routing.go#L1006-L1009

```go
restingUntil.Lock()
restingUntil.m[id] = r.Until
restingUntil.note[id] = r
restingUntil.Unlock()
```

The model-narrowing path a few hundred lines earlier already keeps whichever rest ends later:

https://github.com/yetone/magpie/blob/95be6bb/internal/gateway/routing.go#L546-L549

## Suggested fix

Keep the longer rest when one already in place ends later. At least don't let `failRate` replace a `failCredit` / `failQuota` / `failRestricted` rest that is still active. A 429 that arrives after the account has run out of credit doesn't mean the credit is back.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Use a provider whose balance can't cover one request but is above zero, so it answers `402` to the request it admits and `429` + `Retry-After: 1` to requests running at the same time.
2. Have an agent send 2+ requests at once (e.g. a main turn plus a title or subagent call).
3. Watch the Routing page: the provider's rest keeps flipping between `credit` and a ~1 s `rate` rest, and requests keep going upstream.

comments.body:
A fix is available in my fork: [b7df5885](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/commit/b7df5885929617f648bf8b9022f77938e6bf7e19), branch `fix/rest-deadline-monotonic`.

The shared `restAfterMarked` writer now compares deadlines under the existing lock and keeps the longer rest together with its reason/metadata. This covers account-wide and model-only rest keys. Successful requests, renewed allowance and explicit wakes can still lift a rest.

One important detail: the return value still describes this request's failure. Returning the older rest instead would let `unforbid` mistake a later ordinary 403 for an earlier credit rest and remove the wrong one.

On current base `ca4a1cde`, old code failed the six long-first combinations (credit/quota/restricted × account/model), and the 403 undo regression. Fixed tests passed, including related cases with `-race -count=20 -cpu=1,2`. Current code floors Retry-After:1 at one minute, but it still overwrote the 30-minute rest; the fix addresses that same ordering bug. Vendor traffic was simulated locally, not replayed against sub2tok.

Combined validation: these changes are included in [065f0c8f](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/commit/065f0c8ffc9e30225f3d468ef41ec414aab75e02) on `fix/issue-batch-20261023`. At that exact commit, `go test -tags nogui ./... -count=1 -timeout=45m`, native/Linux/Windows vet and native/Linux/Windows builds all passed with Go 1.26.8, a temporary HOME and pinned Go caches (Linux host, umask 027). Cross-platform builds/vet are not Windows runtime tests. These full-suite results apply to the combined commit; the focused results above apply to the individual fix.

gateway: a shorter rest no longer overwrites a longer one (#3289, wjq990112)

When concurrent requests on one provider fail differently, whichever rest is written last used to win, even if it was shorter. On a sub2tok account whose balance can't cover one request, a `402` `insufficient_balance` rests it for half an hour, while a `429` (`rate_limit_error`, `retry-after: 1`) answering the same moment — the first request still holding the vendor's only slot — rests it for the minute a rate limit starts at. Written about 100 ms apart, the 429's minute replaced the 402's half-hour, and the account was asked again as soon as it ended, refused, and rested again, round after round: the reporter watched some 3,400 refusals in six hours, in bursts of two or three requests every few seconds, with the Routing page's rest flipping between credit and rate.

The write is unconditional. `restAfterMarked` ends with `restingUntil.m[id] = r.Until; restingUntil.note[id] = r` (internal/gateway/routing.go, the `#3289` site), whatever may already rest there. The codebase already keeps the later-ending rest everywhere else it touches this map: `narrowWhenRead` writes a model-narrowed quota rest only when nothing longer stands, and `restSlow` (398803e3) returns the kept rest with "resting longer already, for what another failure said". Nothing pins last-write-wins as intended; a 429 arriving after the account has run out of credit doesn't mean the credit is back.

`restAfterMarked` now writes its rest only when nothing is resting there yet, or when the rest it took ends later than the one in place. A longer rest still replaces a shorter one, a failure whose rest ends later is written as before, and the Rest the function returns still describes the failure that just happened — the trace's try keeps its own why, while `quotaHeld`, `soonestBack` and the Routing page read the map and see the rest that really stands. Rests that lift or shorten by design are untouched: `clearRest` on an answer, `renewed` on windows read full no more, `Unrest`/`UnrestAll` by hand, and the `By: "off"` rests that never reach the map at all.

TestShorterRestDoesNotReplaceLongerOne drives `restAfter` twice on one account: a 402 out of credit, then a 429 with `Retry-After: 1` — the map must still rest by credit, with about `creditRest` left — and then an 8-day `usage_limit_reached` refusal, which must take. Before the fix it went red at "the rate rest replaced the credit rest"; after, green. Broken by hand for the ablation: the guard dropped, the test went red at the same line; restored, green.

Run at the worktree on 398803e3: gofmt -l clean; go vet -tags nogui on darwin, GOOS=linux and GOOS=windows, and go build on darwin, GOOS=linux and GOOS=windows (-tags nogui; the GUI tree itself doesn't cross-compile from this machine, untouched by the patch anyway). The gateway package's full suite with -tags nogui: ok (340.7s), and the new test alone -race -count=3: ok. Not tried: a real sub2tok account behind a near-empty balance; the fixture stubs `allowances` and feeds the vendor's replies to `restAfter` directly.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `go test -tags nogui -run TestShorterRestDoesNotReplaceLongerOne ./internal/gateway`, guard dropped | red: "the rate rest replaced the credit rest" (rest_write_test.go:57) |
| same, fix in | ok |
| `go test -tags nogui -timeout 45m ./internal/gateway` | ok 340.7s |
| `go test -tags nogui -race -count=3 -run TestShorterRestDoesNotReplaceLongerOne ./internal/gateway` | ok |
| `gofmt -l internal/gateway/routing.go internal/gateway/rest_write_test.go` | clean |
| `go vet -tags nogui ./internal/gateway`, darwin / GOOS=linux / GOOS=windows | ok, ok, ok |
| `go build .` darwin; `GOOS=linux` and `GOOS=windows` `go build -tags nogui .` | ok, ok, ok |
| ablation: guard dropped again, test re-run, restored | red at the same line; green after restore; `git status` clean |

```patch
+		rest:  "sub2tok#me@x.com",

+	s.Unrest(acct.restKey())
```

A fix is available in my fork: [b7df5885](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/commit/b7df5885929617f648bf8b9022f77938e6bf7e19), branch `fix/rest-deadline-monotonic`.

The shared `restAfterMarked` writer now compares deadlines under the existing lock and keeps the longer rest together with its reason/metadata. This covers account-wide and model-only rest keys. Successful requests, renewed allowance and explicit wakes can still lift a rest.

One important detail: the return value still describes this request's failure. Returning the older rest instead would let `unforbid` mistake a later ordinary 403 for an earlier credit rest and remove the wrong one.

On current base `ca4a1cde`, old code failed the six long-first combinations (credit/quota/restricted × account/model), and the 403 undo regression. Fixed tests passed, including related cases with `-race -count=20 -cpu=1,2`. Current code floors Retry-After:1 at one minute, but it still overwrote the 30-minute rest; the fix addresses that same ordering bug. Vendor traffic was simulated locally, not replayed against sub2tok.

Combined validation: these changes are included in [065f0c8f](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/commit/065f0c8ffc9e30225f3d468ef41ec414aab75e02) on `fix/issue-batch-20261023`. At that exact commit, `go test -tags nogui ./... -count=1 -timeout=45m`, native/Linux/Windows vet and native/Linux/Windows builds all passed with Go 1.26.8, a temporary HOME and pinned Go caches (Linux host, umask 027). Cross-platform builds/vet are not Windows runtime tests. These full-suite results apply to the combined commit; the focused results above apply to the individual fix.

gateway: a shorter rest no longer overwrites a longer one (#3289, wjq990112)

When concurrent requests on one provider fail differently, whichever rest is written last used to win, even if it was shorter. On a sub2tok account whose balance can't cover one request, a `402` `insufficient_balance` rests it for half an hour, while a `429` (`rate_limit_error`, `retry-after: 1`) answering the same moment — the first request still holding the vendor's only slot — rests it for the minute a rate limit starts at. Written about 100 ms apart, the 429's minute replaced the 402's half-hour, and the account was asked again as soon as it ended, refused, and rested again, round after round: the reporter watched some 3,400 refusals in six hours, in bursts of two or three requests every few seconds, with the Routing page's rest flipping between credit and rate.

The write is unconditional. `restAfterMarked` ends with `restingUntil.m[id] = r.Until; restingUntil.note[id] = r` (internal/gateway/routing.go, the `#3289` site), whatever may already rest there. The codebase already keeps the later-ending rest everywhere else it touches this map: `narrowWhenRead` writes a model-narrowed quota rest only when nothing longer stands, and `restSlow` (398803e3) returns the kept rest with "resting longer already, for what another failure said". Nothing pins last-write-wins as intended; a 429 arriving after the account has run out of credit doesn't mean the credit is back.

`restAfterMarked` now writes its rest only when nothing is resting there yet, or when the rest it took ends later than the one in place. A longer rest still replaces a shorter one, a failure whose rest ends later is written as before, and the Rest the function returns still describes the failure that just happened — the trace's try keeps its own why, while `quotaHeld`, `soonestBack` and the Routing page read the map and see the rest that really stands. Rests that lift or shorten by design are untouched: `clearRest` on an answer, `renewed` on windows read full no more, `Unrest`/`UnrestAll` by hand, and the `By: "off"` rests that never reach the map at all.

TestShorterRestDoesNotReplaceLongerOne drives `restAfter` twice on one account: a 402 out of credit, then a 429 with `Retry-After: 1` — the map must still rest by credit, with about `creditRest` left — and then an 8-day `usage_limit_reached` refusal, which must take. Before the fix it went red at "the rate rest replaced the credit rest"; after, green. Broken by hand for the ablation: the guard dropped, the test went red at the same line; restored, green.

Not tried: a real sub2tok account behind a near-empty balance; the fixture stubs `allowances` and feeds the vendor's replies to `restAfter` directly.

issue.title: Routing treats a readable balance as "allowance not known": providers with balance but no usage windows (e.g. MiniMax Code) always show unknown

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
### What happened

The Routing page shows 「剩余额度未知」 ("remaining allowance not known yet") for providers whose usage API returns a **balance but no windows**, even though magpie successfully read the balance.

**Root cause (verified in source):** `internal/provider/routing.go:502`:

```go
for user, q := range readings {
    if q.Error != "" || len(q.Windows) == 0 {
        continue
    }
    all[user] = allowanceOf(q.Windows, time.Now())...
}
```

A reading with `Windows: []` but a non-empty `Balance` is skipped entirely, so the account is treated as unknown.

**Real-world example (MiniMax Code, from `~/.config/magpie/quotas.json`):**

```json
"minimax-code/minimax336627": {
  "quota": {
    "provider": "minimax-code",
    "plan": "Free",
    "user": "MiniMax336627",
    "windows": [],
    "balance": "1740.72 credits",
    "readAt": "2026-10-23T14:51:39.6466365+08:00"
  }
}
```

The balance **is** read (1,740.72 credits) and even displayed on the Usage/provider page, but the Routing page says 「剩余额度未知」 and the router weights the account as if nothing were known (it falls into the `learns` path).

### Suggested fix

When `len(q.Windows) == 0` but `q.Balance != ""`, still build an `Allowance` — either as an unwindowed meter keyed off the balance text (there is precedent: balance meters already render on the Usage page), or at minimum surface `Known: true` with the balance so routing doesn't treat a readable account as unknown.

Related but distinct: #2333 (expose holds via CLI/JSON), #3193 (custom provider balance meter switch). This issue is specifically about the `Windows == 0 → unknown` branch in the routing path.

```patch
+	if until, ok := restingUntil.m[id]; !ok || !until.After(r.Until) {
+		restingUntil.m[id] = r.Until
+		restingUntil.note[id] = r
+	}
 	restingUntil.Unlock()
 	if unread && id == c.restKey() && id != c.restID() {
 		narrowing.Add(1)
-- 
2.50.1 (Apple Git-155)

```

Branch with the commit: [hunt65-a-3289-rest-max](https://github.com/ggbdpq/magpie/tree/hunt65-a-3289-rest-max) (head `aebfcc6a15a9bbc3b96e0849d045bdf105fb6cad`).

Rebased onto the current main (head `a611bb3c7`). Upstream added the credit-ladder rest persistence on the same lines in the meantime (`kept`/`saveRests`, b4cb946f9), so the merged block keeps the ladder check ahead of the note and applies the patch's longer-rest-wins condition to the writes. Targeted tests green (`TestShorterRestDoesNotReplaceLongerOne`, the rest/ladder family).

Rebased onto the current main (head `606743831`), no conflicts.
New head `d419cab3bd62` (branch `hunt65-a-3289-rest-max`); `git am` clean on `606743831`; patch sha256[:16] `8d5227a9b5b68e1d`.

Landed in v0.1.2497:
- 18387b93b (ggbdpq): a shorter failure (the 1s 429 rest) no longer overwrites a longer rest that's already set (`TestShorterRestDoesNotReplaceLongerOne`).
- 27099f9fc (review follow-up): with that rule alone, a reset time the vendor names couldn't replace magpie's own longer guess for the same quota. A vendor's `resets`/`retry-after` time for the same reason now replaces a guessed rest even when it's sooner (`TestNamedQuotaTimeReplacesAGuess`, red with the condition taken out).

I'm leaving this open until @wjq990112 confirms.

issue.title: [Bug] Claude Desktop retries Claude overflow after successful DeepSeek failover, including within the same turn

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
Claude Desktop repeatedly selects a Claude subscription model that returns `Prompt is too long`, then silently succeeds through DeepSeek. This happens even on two consecutive requests labeled as the same turn. Earlier in the same session, Claude models successfully processed nearly 1M input tokens. Please help investigate the effective limit and repeated retries; the available evidence does **not** establish Extra usage as the root cause.

## Environment

- macOS, Apple Silicon; Magpie 0.1.1364.
- Claude Desktop in third-party Gateway mode, using `group/progressive-vibe-claude` and `typesafe/jev-latest`.
- Environment collected after the incident: Claude Desktop 3.6556.2; Claude Code on PATH 2.1.310. These are collection-time versions, not proof of the exact Desktop/bridge builds used by the earlier failing requests.
- Incidents below occurred on 2026-10-24, UTC+08:00. All five rows belong to the **same original session**, anonymized as `session-A`.
- The selected routes identify one Claude subscription account, labeled Pro. The local account cache matches that account; its identity is omitted.

## Observed behavior

1. A long-running Desktop Code conversation uses the routing group.
2. The intent rule selects Sonnet or another Claude model.
3. That attempt returns `400`, `fail: overflow`, `Prompt is too long`.
4. Another member succeeds, so Desktop receives a final `200`. Routing shows a rejected Claude attempt but no client-visible error.
5. Subsequent requests again attempt Claude before falling back. Two consecutive records below both identify the selected rule's turn as **106**.

This was extracted from real routing logs, not a synthetic reproduction. No private conversation or production request was replayed to prepare this report.

## Sanitized log evidence

`tokens_field` is the routing record's `rule.tokens`. `reported_input` is calculated from the **successful member's** usage (`in + cache_read + cache_write`). Neither is presented as an authoritative count of the input received by a failed Claude attempt.

| Time (+08:00) | Request ID | Turn | Attempts, in order | Successful member's reported input |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 14:10:02.528 | 1792822157213 | 101 | Sonnet 400 / overflow in 66 ms; Opus 200 | Opus: 2 + 977,558 cache read + 20,766 cache write = **998,326** |
| 14:10:36.519 | 1792822157214 | 101 | Opus 400 / overflow in 65 ms; Sonnet 200 | Sonnet: 2 + 996,343 cache read + 2,269 cache write = **998,614** |
| 14:11:29.999 | 1792822157217 | 102 | Haiku 400 / overflow; Sonnet 400 / overflow; Opus 400 / overflow; DeepSeek 200 | DeepSeek: 607,721 + 62,336 cache read = **670,057** |
| 14:16:58.672 | 1792822157237 | 106 | Sonnet 400 / overflow in 3,395 ms; DeepSeek 200 | DeepSeek: 184 + 674,048 cache read = **674,232** |
| 14:17:10.559 | 1792822157238 | 106 | Sonnet 400 / overflow in 4,544 ms; DeepSeek 200 | DeepSeek: 521 + 674,688 cache read = **675,209** |

The last row corresponds to the screenshot's approximately 676.1K total tokens: 675,209 input + 906 output = 676,115. That is **DeepSeek's usage**, not a measurement proving what Sonnet received.

Representative routing excerpts (allowlisted fields only):

```json
{"request_id":1792822157237,"session":"session-A","time":"2026-10-24T14:16:58.6726+08:00","rule":{"n":5,"turn":106,"use":"claude/claude-sonnet-5-5","tokens_field":673268},"affinity":{"mode":"session","last":"deepseek","lastTurn":105,"why":"rule"},"tries":[{"model":"claude-sonnet-5-5","status":400,"fail":"overflow","error":"Prompt is too long","ms":3395},{"model":"deepseek-flash","status":200,"ms":6638}],"status":200,"usage":[{"provider":"deepseek","model":"deepseek-flash","in":184,"out":576,"cache_read":674048}]}
{"request_id":1792822157238,"session":"session-A","time":"2026-10-24T14:17:10.559608+08:00","rule":{"n":5,"turn":106,"use":"claude/claude-sonnet-5-5","held":true,"tokens_field":674232},"affinity":{"mode":"session","within":true,"last":"deepseek","lastTurn":106,"why":"rule"},"tries":[{"model":"claude-sonnet-5-5","status":400,"fail":"overflow","error":"Prompt is too long","ms":4544},{"model":"deepseek-flash","status":200,"ms":9996}],"status":200,"usage":[{"provider":"deepseek","model":"deepseek-flash","in":521,"out":906,"cache_read":674688}]}
```

Some earlier failures (including the first three rows' fast failures) include Magpie's extended explanation identifying a **Claude Code local preflight check**, with the conditional explanation about an account requiring Extra usage for long context. Other attempts only say `Prompt is too long`. The failed-attempt records do not include an upstream maximum or a Claude-side input token count.

## Configuration and uncertainty

The current settings were collected **after** the incidents and have changed during troubleshooting; they are not an exact historical reproduction fixture:

```json
{
  "magpie": {
    "fullContext": true,
    "desktopLongest": true,
    "group_affinity": "session",
    "group_context": -1
  },
  "current_desktop_group_catalog": {
    "id": "mythos-magpie-7447083768",
    "max_input_tokens": 500000,
    "max_output_tokens": 393216
  },
  "current_claude_settings": {
    "env": {"CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONTEXT_TOKENS": "1048576"},
    "modelSettings": {
      "mythos-magpie-7447083768": {"autoCompactWindow": 400000}
    }
  }
}
```

The local Claude account cache currently has `hasExtraUsageEnabled: false` and `cachedExtraUsageDisabledReason: "org_level_disabled"`. These are **cached flags**, not a live verification of billing policy or evidence that Anthropic returned the long-context Extra usage rejection for the specific attempts above. The earlier successful Claude usage near 1M also makes a blanket statement that this account always has a 200K window insufficient.

## Expected behavior / questions

- Preserve successful fallback, but avoid repeatedly trying a member known not to fit the current conversation when no relevant condition changed.
- Please check why failover did not appear to stick across the two records labeled turn 106. Does the trace turn ID imply the same turn for this behavior, and is a new intent/rule decision overriding the successful member?
- Distinguish the routing estimate, each member's effective limit, and the final successful member's reported input in diagnostics. A single healthy context meter can otherwise obscure the rejected member's actual limit.
- Determine whether this is a retained Claude Code process/account limit, a request transformation/resume discrepancy, or a context/compaction metadata problem before recommending paid Extra usage or a global reduction to 200K.
- If no member can accept the request, preserve an overflow response the client can recognize and compact on. Do not turn on paid usage or silently discard history as a fix.

Possibly related: #2162 (Claude Code local preflight explanation), #1404 (the successful member supplies the displayed count), and #3348 (learning effective limits after overflow). This report is specifically about the Claude subscription bridge with Desktop and the contradictory success/failure evidence above; I have not established a shared root cause with those issues.

Emails, account identifiers, local paths, original session UUIDs, credentials, request headers, private prompts, custom intent text, and tool payloads are omitted. I have retained a local JSON extraction with these five records and source line references.
